abstract: In our previous work [H.-S. Cho, Phys. Rev. D 105. 124022 (2022)], we studied the impact of eccentricity on gravitational-wave parameter estimation for a nonspinning binary neutron star (BNS) system. We here extend the work to a general binary system by including the spin parameter. As in the previous work, we employ the analytic Fisher-Cutler-Vallisneri method to calculate the systematic bias that can be produced by using noneccentric waveforms in parameter estimation, and we verify the reliability of the method by comparing it with numerical Bayesian parameter estimation results. We generate <math display="inline"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></math> BNS sources randomly distributed in the parameter space <math display="inline"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>–</mi><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>–</mi><msub><mi>χ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mi>–</mi><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>, where the neutron star mass is in the range of <math display="inline"><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">⊙</mo></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">⊙</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, the effective spin is <math display="inline"><mo>-</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>χ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.2</mn></math>, and the eccentricity (at the reference frequency 10 Hz) is <math display="inline"><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.024</mn></math>. For the true value of the tidal deformability (<math display="inline"><mi>λ</mi></math>) of neutron stars, we assume the equation of state model APR4. For all gravitational-wave signals emitted from the sources, we calculate the systematic biases (<math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></math>) for the chirp mass (<math display="inline"><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></math>), symmetric mass ratio (<math display="inline"><mi>η</mi></math>), effective spin (<math display="inline"><msub><mi>χ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub></math>), and effective tidal deformability (<math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover></math>), and obtain generalized distributions of the biases. The distribution of biases in <math display="inline"><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi></math>, and <math display="inline"><msub><mi>χ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub></math> shows narrow bands, and the median value of the bias increases or decreases quadratically with increasing <math display="inline"><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>, indicating a weak dependence of biases on the three parameters. On the other hand, the biases of <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover></math> are widely distributed depending on the values of the mass and spin parameters at a given <math display="inline"><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. We investigate the implications of biased parameters for the inference of neutron star properties by performing Bayesian parameter estimation for specific cases. We find that a BNS signal consisting of two neutron stars within the typical mass range <math display="inline"><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">⊙</mo></msub></math> can be estimated to be a BNS signal whose component mass is much smaller or much larger than the typical mass range. In particular, by showing concrete examples, we demonstrate that parameter estimation using noneccentric waveforms for eccentric BNS signals can yield false predictions for the neutron star equation of state.
title: Systematic bias due to eccentricity in parameter estimation for merging binary neutron stars : spinning case
